subject: character_name_table_fields
claim: On revision r806919.Wizard_1_610, each disallowed-name row is a DisallowedName object with five unsigned-int fields, linked from the DisallowedNameList object's m_disallowedNameList collection.
how_to_repeat: Run typeextract against your own r806919.Wizard_1_610 install and inspect the DisallowedNameList and DisallowedName class properties in its JSON type dump.
Compare the dump's property names, types, and order with the registered fields in Ambrose's NameViews.h.
Run extractor --client <install> --type-dump <dump> --dry-run names and confirm that it reads the local disallowed-name list without reporting an extraction error.
evidence: The local type dump identifies revision r806919.Wizard_1_610 and contains 6,986 class entries.
The dump's class DisallowedNameList has one reflected property, m_disallowedNameList, with type class SharedPointer<class DisallowedName>.
The dump's class DisallowedName has exactly five properties in order: m_locale, m_gender, m_first, m_middle, and m_last; each is unsigned int.
Ambrose's DisallowedNameView registers those same five unsigned-int fields in that order, and ReadDisallowed reads them into each row while assigning its Id from the list position.
The offline extractor dry run against the local install and matching type dump completed successfully and reported four disallowed-name rows; no name values are included here.
disproof: A repeat on the same revision that finds a different list property, a different row field name, type, or order in the dump, or that shows the extractor reads a different row shape, refutes this claim.
